subject: Crestline Health - elevated 429s and token latency causing throttling
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@crestline.health>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.p@crestline.health>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden 429s + 3-5s token latency spike (we're blocked)

Ava —

We're seeing a sudden spike of 429s and token-level latency jumping to 3-5s on our production calls since ~08:45 PT. Throughput is dropping and retries are making behavior worse. This started right after we increased concurrency on our worker pool this morning as part of a scheduled rollout. Our service is now intermittently failing a subset of auth'ed requests.

Can you confirm whether any quota or burst policy changed on your side? We haven't touched API keys or traffic shaping. This is impacting our payment flows and we need an ETA — customers are affected.

Attaching a short log snippet.

— Liam
Senior Platform Engineer, Crestline Health

Attachment: crestline_request_spike_20270401.log (text, 87KB)
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@crestline.health>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 429s + 3-5s token latency spike (we're blocked)

Liam — thanks for the heads up and the log. I'm escalating immediately. I'm looping in Neha from Customer Ops and Marissa (VP) since this is high-impact.

Quick asks while we investigate:
- Can you share whether the increased concurrency used the same API keys/tenant?
- Any spike in payload size or embeddings calls?

Neha and I will run a parallel investigation on quota windowing, burst credits, and routing. We'll update within 30 minutes with a mitigations plan.

Ava
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@crestline.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 429s + 3-5s token latency spike (we're blocked)

Liam / Ava — initial findings from ops: we saw a sustained burst of high-frequency short-lived requests starting 08:43 PT tied to the tenant key used in the logs you sent. The platform's burst-credit controller exhausted the tenant burst bucket and started applying per-window QPS enforcement which produced the 429s. Simultaneously, request routing fell back to a secondary model variant with higher token execution time, which explains token-level latency increases.

Planned mitigations (immediate):
1) Temporarily increase Crestline's burst window by +2x for 30 minutes to allow their rollout to finish (will apply within 5 minutes).
2) Put an emergency routing override to pin requests to the lower-latency model variant while we stabilize.
3) Add a targeted cache warm path for their common prefixes to reduce token work.

I'll attach a CSV of token metrics and the canary-config diff for the routing override. We'll monitor and follow up in 15 minutes. If this persists, we'll propose a short rollback for their internal rollout.

Attachments: crestline_token_metrics_20270401.csv, canary-config-diff.patch

Neha Kapoor
Customer Reliability (Ops), Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 429s + 3-5s token latency spike (we're blocked)

Team — thanks for fast triage. I'm elevating to exec: copying Connor (SRE lead) and scheduling an urgent sync with CTO and Head of Product in 30 minutes.

Items for the sync:
- Confirmed root cause (burst-credit exhaustion + fallback routing to higher-latency model variant).
- Immediate customer impact: payment path failures; ~12% of requests returning 429 over 20 minutes.
- Short-term mitigation (Neha's plan): increase burst allowance + routing override.
- Ask for SRE: evaluate why fallback routing tripped (was it capacity-aware or misclassification?) and verify canary-config autopromote timing.

Connor — can you prepare a 1-slide RCA draft and include any guardrail changes we should push today (e.g., telemetry thresholds that auto-block hazard rollouts)?

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 429s + 3-5s token latency spike (we're blocked)

Marissa / team — SRE update: we've identified a logic gap in the burst-credit replenishment scheduler where a tenant-level concurrency flag set by the customer's rollout caused the replenishment to skip that tenant for 10 windows. That allowed burst credits to be consumed without timely replenishment. We're rolling a hotfix to the scheduler now; estimated deploy in 20 minutes.

Immediate actions completed:
- Applied temporary burst window increase for Crestline (verified in ops).
- Pinned routing to the low-latency variant (verified).
- Deployed a temporary guard in the canary controller to prevent autopromote for this tenant until we complete validation.

I'll post a short post-mortem and the patch (INF-7123) after the hotfix.

-Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@crestline.health>, Sara Patel <sara.p@crestline.health>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 17:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 429s + 3-5s token latency spike (we're blocked) — mitigation complete

Liam / Sara — following up with a status update and next steps.

What we did (summary):
- Identified root cause: tenant burst-credit scheduler skipped replenishment windows for your tenant when you temporarily raised concurrency, exhausting burst credits and triggering per-window QPS enforcement.
- Mitigations applied: temporary +2x burst allowance, routing pinned to lower-latency variant, and a hotfix to scheduler (deployed 16:58 PT) to address the replenishment gap.
- Impact: 429s reduced from ~12% to <0.5% within 10 minutes; token latency returned to baseline.

Next steps (with owners):
- Karthik / SRE: permanent scheduler fix + regression test (INF-7123) — ETA 48 hours.
- Neha / Customer Ops: follow up with a tailored quota profile and guidance for safe concurrency ramping — ETA 24 hours.
- Ava / Solutions: schedule a brief post-incident review with Crestline to align rollout guidance and offer sandboxed ramp plan — suggested time tomorrow.

We apologize for the disruption. If you'd like, we can keep a dedicated war-room channel while we complete the follow-ups.

Thanks for your partnership — we appreciate your patience.

Best,
Ava Chen
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
